equivalent_not_counted.argument: equivalent: within one directory file names are unique, so a source name occurs once per directory and the first-of-name rule across directories (directory order, not name order) decides; reversing the in-directory order cannot change which descriptor wins (R90MMutC1 §7-C).

equivalent through routing: the only plain_string caller is DBusName, and a DBusName that is not valid UTF-8 fails the bus-name grammar (`is_bus_name` accepts only [A-Za-z_-][A-Za-z0-9_-]* elements) with or without _check_utf8, so the descriptor is skipped either way (cases b93-ac0af-portal-dbusname, r93-nul-portal-dbusname-tail pick identically).

equivalent through routing (R92MExecD1 §(d)): both readers look keys up by exact name and never strip a locale suffix, so a kept `x[C]`/`x[c]` is the literal key `x[C]`/`x[c]` and can never match `x`; whether it is kept or dropped is invisible to a pick (cases d1-d4, b93-d-*).

not_counted_survivors.argument: unkillable in this shape on the current bytes: accepting an unterminated `[group` line sends parse_keyfile to `s[1:s.rindex("]")]`, which raises ValueError (uncaught, the tool exits nonzero on mc-n19-unterminated-group; reproduced as `ValueError: substring not found` at parse_keyfile), and a crash is not a kill (QUALITY 148). The rule itself is still covered by M29 (trailing text after the bracket) and the candidate passes mc-n19.

not equivalent in principle but unkillable and inadmissible: no frozen case gives an Encoding value a byte outside ASCII without also giving one to a read list value, where `encode('utf-8')` and `encode('utf-8','surrogateescape')` differ only by raising UnicodeEncodeError — the mutant crashes on r93-encoding-invalid-first-group and r93-encoding-later-group (2 crashes, 0 wrong answers), and a crash is not a kill (QUALITY 148).
